stem: Input EC is stable, but root-zone EC rises as containers are allowed to dry much more deeply between irrigations. Which interpretation is strongest?
choices: The fertilizer concentrate probably changed despite stable input EC, because concentrate composition can shift without altering conductivity and should be reformulated before irrigation changes
Lower root-zone water content can concentrate dissolved ions, so moisture pattern and possible salt accumulation should be evaluated together
The EC increase most likely indicates developing root disease, because diseased roots release enough ions to raise substrate conductivity
A change in source-water pH is probably responsible, because root-zone EC generally rises only after the incoming pH has shifted
rationale: As root-zone water content declines, dissolved ions can become more concentrated. EC trends should therefore be interpreted together with moisture status and irrigation behavior.
